name: Morgan ab Athrwys
summary:
Morgan ap Athrwys was a king of Gwent and Glywysing in southeast Wales, reigning from approximately 1063 to 1092. His reign is notable for the establishment of a stable and prosperous Welsh state, which he maintained through strategic alliances and military victories.

Ap Athrwys' most significant achievement was his successful resistance against the Norman invasion of Wales, led by Robert Fitzhamon, in 1071. This victory allowed him to maintain control over his kingdom and preserve Welsh independence for several decades.

The legacy of Morgan ap Athrwys can be seen in the continued prosperity and stability of Gwent and Glywysing during the 12th century. His reign also laid the foundation for future Welsh kingdoms, including the Principality of Wales, which emerged in the 13th century.

As a testament to his enduring impact, Morgan ap Athrwys' name remains synonymous with Welsh strength and resilience, inspiring generations of Welsh leaders and patriots.

The historical significance of Morgan ap Athrwys can be measured by his ability to resist Norman aggression and preserve Welsh sovereignty, earning him a place among the most important figures in Welsh history.
